sections.title: Strategic Writing for Fundraising
sections.description: Developing a targeted strategy for individual prospects and/or donors is critical, but communicating it effectively is what gets you over the finish line. In this course, we will explore how to successfully apply strategic communications approaches to real-life scenarios. You will learn about the continuous cycle of fundraising and get practice and coaching on how to write the full spectrum of donor-centric communication vehicles relevant to each cycle. Strategic Writing for Fundraising Professionals will walk you through case studies, share some tricks of the trade, focus on specific challenges, and provide feedback on your writing throughout. Expect to be enlightened, engaged, and pushed to think hard about how you communicate to build the productive relationships that result in impactful philanthropy.

sections.title: Strategic Writing for Fundraising
sections.description:
Whether seeking support for an initiative, advancing a cause, securing resources, or persuading others to invest in an idea, professionals must know how to make a compelling case for action. Fundraising offers an especially rich opportunity to develop these skills because it brings together many of the most demanding elements of persuasive writing: understanding audiences, establishing credibility and trust, appealing to values and interests, and combining evidence, reasoning, and emotion to motivate action.
This course uses fundraising as a practical laboratory for studying and practicing effective persuasion. Students learn to analyze audiences, frame persuasive messages, develop compelling cases for support, anticipate objections, and inspire action without coercion. Throughout, the course emphasizes the ethical and strategic dimensions of persuasion, including the importance of building relationships and communicating with clarity, purpose, and credibility.
Although the course focuses on fundraising, the writing strategies students develop extend well beyond philanthropy. They are equally valuable in advocacy, leadership, consulting, marketing, public policy, nonprofit and corporate communications, and other professional contexts in which success depends on persuading others to support ideas, initiatives, and organizations.
